graphic_pad_basis: each part's pad copper against every OTHER part's footprint graphic copper (fp_poly / fp_line / fp_arc / fp_rect / fp_circle on a copper layer, #908) on a shared layer: the strokes by check_drc's pad-to-segment test, a filled shape's interior by containment (#1181). A CONTACT is judged on the stroke as drawn and is a `stack` on ANY net (two parts' copper in one place, check_assembly's pad_intersection argument) except a net tie's own tied net on the tie's copper; the clearance shortfall is graded at the modelled stroke check_drc grades and skips a pad of the one net the copper's owner gives it. Board-level art is not measured, nor copper the parser does not model (graphic_copper_unmeasured)
keepout_copper_unmeasured_after: footprint-owned rule area: moves with its part and is not re-posed by placement, so it is not graded
legal_basis: legal = measured pad/hole/outline channels (pad copper AND footprint graphic copper) are clean, no two parts' pads are stacked (any net), and edge coverage is complete; no_worse = no measured category worsened relative to the input board. Neither verifies what legal_unmeasured lists.
legal_scope: pad copper vs the edge-clearance floor
footprint graphic copper vs the outline
pad copper vs a board rule-area keep-out band (#1031)
part bodies vs a PCB-edge plug's mating region (#1098)
pad copper vs ANOTHER part's footprint graphic copper (a drawn SOT-89 tab, an antenna), its filled interior included: short of clearance on a net it is not, or touching on any net (#1266)
two parts' pad copper overlapping on a shared side, ANY net -- a pad stack, check_assembly's pad_intersection (#1064)
one footprint's own pads touching on two different real nets (KiCad's shorting_items; #1306)
legal_unmeasured: footprint graphic copper vs the edge-clearance floor (disclosed as graphic_edge_shortfall_refs, not gated)
footprint copper the parser does not model: pad-less logos, bezier curves, copper text (named per part in oob_graphic_copper_unmeasured)
footprint graphic copper on a board with no outline, and on a part that changed side in memory (listed as no-outline / moved-side in oob_graphic_copper_unmeasured)
rule areas a footprint owns (listed in keepout_copper_unmeasured)
parts sharing an origin whose pads do not intersect (check_assembly's coincident_origins)
oob_pad_basis: part pad AABB vs outline inflated by the grading clearance (NOT the per-pad outline measure; see render_placement checklist.a_off_outline.pad_copper)
own_pad_basis: each footprint's own pads against each other, by check_drc's pad-to-pad test, on a shared copper layer. Exempt as KiCad exempts them: two pads on one net, two pads with one number (unless they carry two different real nets that are not both a pin's `unconnected-(...)` net), and two pads in one net_tie_pad_groups group. Two pads with no net are not graded (check_drc's same-net rule; KiCad grades them `clearance`). A `short` is a contact between two pads on real nets (KiCad: shorting_items); a contact with a no-net pad is `no_net` (KiCad: clearance, actual 0)

pad_edge_after.basis: analytic pad copper extrema (custom pads: parsed polygons) vs rectangular Edge.Cuts centreline (within 0.1 mm of one: its bbox shrunk by the outline_inset_mm it strays); edge-straddling castellated pads exempt; other outlines sampled, not certified; no body/track/via/fill check

unmeasured.reason: simplified pad geometry: chamfered pad; outline uses sampled perimeter check

pad_edge_before.basis: analytic pad copper extrema (custom pads: parsed polygons) vs rectangular Edge.Cuts centreline (within 0.1 mm of one: its bbox shrunk by the outline_inset_mm it strays); edge-straddling castellated pads exempt; other outlines sampled, not certified; no body/track/via/fill check

unmeasured.reason: simplified pad geometry: chamfered pad; outline uses sampled perimeter check

pad_stack_basis: check_assembly's pad_intersection channel (legality.pad_intersection_pairs): two parts' pad copper intersecting on a shared side, any net, confirmed on the pads' outlines by check_drc's pad-pad check; never waivable
